name: High-pass phaser chord pad: saw chords through a heavily resonant high-pass whose cutoff is automated, ping-pong 1/4 delay and a big reverb both low-cut at about 200 Hz, a phaser on a slow 2-bar cycle, a harmonizer shifted to the 3rd harmonic for a bell tone, unison and light compression
goal: Make moving chords or a pad from a plain saw wave using a high-pass filter and a phaser (works in any synth with these, or as post-processing on a saw). Play low chords on a single saw. Add a high-pass filter with resonance turned way up and automate its cutoff to sweep the chord's movement. Add a ping-pong delay at 1/4 note with a low cut around 200 Hz (so the bass isn't muddy) and some stereo spread, then a large reverb, also low-cut about 200 Hz, with size up, slightly longer decay, damping and wet up. Add a phaser set to complete one cycle every 2 bars (its direction sets whether it sweeps up or down) for slow top-end motion. Add a harmonizer (octave copies) with amount and width high, then shift its interval from the octave to the 3rd harmonic for a bell-like tone. Add unison voices to taste, light compression, and pull the highs and some mids down a little.

prerequisites: Any synth (or DAW FX) with a resonant high-pass filter, phaser with tempo-synced rate, ping-pong delay, reverb; harmonic or octave stacking (harmonizer or extra oscillators) optional

inputs.name: tempo
inputs.description: Project tempo for syncing the 2-bar phaser cycle

outputs.name: patch
outputs.description: Portable recipe for the high-pass phaser chord pad

constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.
The phaser 'one cycle per 2 bars' is a tempo-synced rate (e.g. 32 sixteenths); set it in your phaser's sync units.
Without a harmonizer, approximate the 3rd-harmonic bell by layering a sine or saw at +19 semitones (octave + fifth) quietly.
Phaser-pad coverage in the library is near-exhausted; this adds the resonant-high-pass-as-motion plus 3rd-harmonic bell variant only.
Auto-generated YouTube Show transcript; partly garbled, values approximate from transcript description.

steps.action: Play low chords on a single saw oscillator.
Insert a high-pass with resonance very high; automate its cutoff across the chords.
steps.expect: Resonant, vocal-like movement inside the chord.

steps.action: Add a ping-pong 1/4-note delay with a ~200 Hz low cut and some extra stereo width.
Add a big reverb: low cut ~200 Hz, size up, decay slightly up, damping up, wet up.
steps.expect: A large wash under the movement.

steps.action: Add a phaser synced to one full cycle per 2 bars; choose its sweep direction (up or down).
Add harmonic stacking: harmonizer amount and width high, interval shifted from the octave to the 3rd harmonic.
steps.expect: A bell-like shimmer above the chord.

steps.action: Add unison voices to taste, light compression, and pull the highs and some mids down slightly.

verification: The high-pass automation is audible as movement on a sustained chord.
The phaser completes exactly one cycle every 2 bars at project tempo.
There is no low-end mud from the delay or reverb (both low-cut).
